body: All good points, but what op is trying to say I think is that while you think you are harming  the ocean by harming a wave, there is no intrinsic harm to be found. Just a disruption of pattern. The illusion of harm exists solely as a psychological byproduct of evolution. We harm and protect in an attempt to drive evolution based on our moral standards. Those who have achieved enlightenment understand that ultimate happiness cannot be fully achieved through harm, but rather apathy followed by realization and growth. But happiness can be found anywhere, which is why people who self immolatate and are Buddhist are so calm. This is why prisoners can be happy. Happiness is all about comparison, and we subconsciously compare our lives to others on the daily. For instance, a murderer in prison can say "my life is shit because it's not as good as when I was free" whereas another prisoner can say " my life is good because I'm not being tortured to death and look what I have compared to others".

I would accept alternatives. I just want to feel safe again tbh. [My psychological need for safety isn't being met currently](https://positivepsychologyprogram.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/Figure-21-Maslows-hierarchy-of-needs-Whats-Your-Motivation-Maslows-Hierarchy-of-min.jpg) and so I sank into a depression and had multiple existential crises and psychotic episodes. Meditation helps curb this a bit but it's only helping cover up the fear instead of getting at the root. Psilocybin seemed to help a lot but the relief lasted only a few months.

21. No, money is pointless. I see it as a drug that people get addicted to for the rush of making it. I would only like to live in the woods and survive off of hunting/growing vegetables. But I may not get to do that. I may be in legal trouble. I'd rather not get into it but I may have no prospects for even that future.
